sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1984, as amended by the 2013 Protocol)
France-United States Double Taxation Convention (1967, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols and the MLI)
France-United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (2008, effective 2009)
France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended by the 2015 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-1 to L561-50 and L561-45 to L561-50 (AML/CFT obligations and French UBO register); Décret n°2016-1805 of 14 December 2016 (UBO declaration and registration); Décret n°2018-284 of 18 April 2018; Ordonnance n°2020-115 of 12 February 2020 (transposing MLD5).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statuts) of each direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign registry of incorporation or notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (if non-Hague Convention jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or corporate extract equivalent to a French Kbis
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar / Trade registry of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the UBO's country of residence (certified true-copy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax Residency Certificate (Attestation de résidence fiscale) of each UBO holding at least 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the country of residence of the UBO

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign registrar or secretary of state of the jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU sanctions lists (Council Implementing Regulation), OFAC SDN List, French national freezing measures (DG Trésor), and TRACFIN typologies. PEPs are identified under Code monétaire et financier Article R561-15 and include domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence applies for high-risk third countries per FATF. Any discrepancy in UBO data must be reported to TRACFIN without delay.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with name clearance verified against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin alphabetic characters. Any non-Latin script term must be transliterated into Latin characters. French law (Ordonnance n°2004-670 on the use of the French language) requires that registration filings and official documents be in French; a foreign-language denotation must be accompanied by a French version in all filings submitted to the Guichet unique.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Crédit (when used in a banking context)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of receipt of a rejection notice from the Guichet unique / INPI, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration, accompanied by a legal memorandum and a prior search of the RNE/RCS and French trademarks. If refusal is maintained, the applicant may initiate summary proceedings before the competent Tribunal de Commerce or Tribunal Judiciaire on grounds of abusive refusal or manifest error, and may alternatively file a new application for a different permissible name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible solely through an approved business domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) authorised to receive official notifications and maintain corporate records in France. A purely digital address without any physical French presence is not permissible; the domiciliation provider must be contractually engaged under Code de commerce Article L123-11-1 and the SARL's commercial substance must be accessible at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the first tax year; estimated annual risk of unannounced inspection by French tax authorities, URSSAF, DGCCRF, or labour inspectorate at 5-8%. This industry (ISIC 4791 internet retail of outdoor gear) is not a priority inspection sector unless VAT anomalies or dissolution risk indicators are detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory publication of incorporation notice in a legal gazette (annonce légale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal-gazette publisher (JAL) in the département of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff established by the relevant legal-notice decree

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SARL articles of association (rédaction des statuts) by a French avocat
UBO declaration preparation and notarized certification of shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff + market rate for AML support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate and UBO documents (five sets)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin / French consulate
Registered business domiciliation company approved by the préfecture / regional authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RNE / RCS filing, greffe taxes, and mandatory registration levies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for company registration under Code de commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening database queries for all UBOs and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party KYC/AML data provider (e.g., LexisNexis, World-Check)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL); Décret n°84-406 of 30 April 1984 on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; Decree 2021-300 on the Guichet Unique formalities system
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), acting through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) filed via the electronic Mo / formalities dossier transmitted to the Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the shareholders freely determine the amount (customarily €1–€100). Where capital is €10,000 or less, the entire amount must be paid up at subscription; where it exceeds €10,000, at least 20% must be paid at formation and the balance within five years. Funds must be deposited in a blocked, interest-bearing account at a French credit institution or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and are released only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [COMPANY NAME] SARL. RESOLVED FIRST: that the Articles of Association are adopted without amendment and the subscribed share capital is fully allocated to the founding shareholder, with contributions deposited in a blocked account. RESOLVED SECOND: that the registered office is fixed at the address set forth in the Articles, and the General Manager is authorized to execute any lease or domiciliation agreement. RESOLVED THIRD: that [Name] is hereby appointed General Manager for an indefinite term, endowed with the widest powers in accordance with Article L.223-18 of the French Commercial Code. RESOLVED FOURTH: that the General Manager may complete all incorporation formalities, open corporate bank accounts, and commence online retail operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Articles of Association and reserve the corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (for name verification) / drafting by a corporate legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the Statuts covering legal form, share capital, share transfer rules, manager powers, and registered office. Perform a name availability search on the INPI database and formally reserve the proposed corporate name.
required_dossiers: Statement of intended activity (internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment, ISIC 4791)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts, promptly amend the reserve application with a secondary name. Any deficiency in the draft Statuts is corrected before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit the subscribed share capital in a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the full subscribed capital from the shareholders' bank accounts and obtain the banker's certificate of blocked capital deposit (Attestation de dépôt des fonds pour compte de la société en formation).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application, deposit the funds with another licensed French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. Where insufficient funds are remitted, increase the payment or revise the stated capital by amending the draft Statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sign the Articles of Association and appoint the General Manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional but recommended) or all shareholders in original form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founding shareholders for signature of the final Statuts. Execute the deed, list the subscribed shares, and record the appointment of the Gérant (General Manager), including the manager's formal acceptance of office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signature or declaration is incomplete, rectify by way of a supplementary deed signed by all parties. A defective acceptance by the manager is cured by signing a new deed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal formation notice (Avis de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Send the notice of incorporation for publication in an approved legal gazette. The notice must state the corporate form, capital, registered office, business purpose, manager identity, and the RCS where registration will occur.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requests corrections, submit a revised notice within 24 hours. Where publication is delayed, select an alternative accredited JAL to meet the filing deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier through the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (coordinating the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the digital formalities dossier (equivalent of the historic M0 form) via guichet-unique.inpi.fr, attaching the Statuts, certificate of capital deposit, proof of legal publication, registered-office domiciliation agreement, and identity documents of officers. Pay the greffe and formalities fees online.
required_dossiers: Certificate of blocked capital deposit from the bank
Proof of registered office (lease, domiciliation agreement, or ownership title)
Identity document and address proof of the General Manager
Declaration of no conviction (form AC1 equivalent)
Power of attorney, if filed through a representative
Domiciliation contract for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Greffe issues a deficiency notice (avis de rejet ou de complément) if the file is incomplete; respond within the statutory 15-day cure period with the missing documents or corrections. If the Greffe maintains the refusal, appeal to the President of the Commercial Court for a registration order under Article 31 of Décret n°84-406.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the K-bis extract and open the operational bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / infogreffe.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Greffe registers the SARL and issues the official French corporate extract (Extrait K-bis), which certifies legal existence, corporate identity, managers, and registered office. Use the K-bis to open a permanent business bank account and to commence e-commerce operations on Stripe and PayPal.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract issued by the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis extract contains errors, file a request for administrative correction with the Greffe; where the extract is delayed, follow up via the Guichet Unique dashboard and request expedition. A verified K-bis is required for bank account opening; until then, the blocked account remains custodied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF) for consumer product safety and e-commerce compliance; Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) for workplace regulation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing license required — the online retail of outdoor camping equipment (ISIC 4791) is activity-neutral under French commercial law and is opened by simple RCS registration; compliance is limited to general product safety (EU GPSR), REACH/CLP obligations, textile labelling rules, and the AGEC Law packaging and e-waste extended-producer-responsibility (EPR) duties.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure e-commerce retail without manufacturing or product transformation; no formal EIA required. Logistics and storage premises are subject to ICPE registration only where a warehouse exceeds 1,500 m² (rubrique 1510), which is outside the anticipated operational scale.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC discharge generated by the retail activity. Compliance applies to product-level environmental rules: batteries and electronic equipment sold as camping gear must meet EU WEEE and RoHS restrictions; packaging must comply with Article L.541-10 of the French Environmental Code and the AGEC Law, including registered take-back schemes (Citeo and ecosystem) and the obligation to register on the ADEME SINOE/EPR portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local SDIS fire authority for the administrative and storage premises; compliance with the French Labour Code (Articles R.4227-1 et seq.) covering means of escape, extinguishers, employee information, and evacuation drills. Structural load inspection certificates are required if racked storage exceeds standard floor ratings. No ERP (public access building) clearance is triggered where the facility is not open to the public; a simple workplace opening declaration is sufficient. Third-party logistics must hold their own valid ICPE status.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official tax portal impots.gouv.fr. Business formation and enterprise identifiers are administered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the SARL through the INPI Guichet unique; the formalities are transmitted to the Registre national des entreprises. 2. Obtain the SIREN enterprise number and SIRET establishment number from INSEE. 3. Open the enterprise tax account on impots.gouv.fr and identify the competent SIE. 4. Submit the VAT registration information, expected turnover, activity description, commencement date, establishment details, bank information, and applicable VAT regime. 5. The SIE assigns the French VAT identification number, generally in the format FR plus a two-digit control key and the SIREN number. 6. For a non-established EU business making French taxable supplies, apply directly to the competent French tax service or use the applicable Union OSS regime where eligible. 7. A non-EU business generally must appoint a French fiscal representative unless a statutory exemption or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. 8. Obtain an EORI number separately through French customs for import and export operations; an EORI is not a VAT number. 9. Register for OSS through the tax authority of the relevant EU Member State where eligible for cross-border B2C supplies. 10. Maintain registration evidence, VAT returns, invoices, customs records, payment evidence, and statutory accounting records for the applicable retention period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). A SARL meeting the statutory conditions may elect for income tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, or IR), including the family SARL regime for qualifying family-owned companies. A newly formed SARL may, subject to ownership, size, age, activity, and shareholder requirements, elect temporary IR treatment for up to five financial years. France has no general United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, include income, or neutralize arrangements producing deduction-without-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT. French domestic retail sales of outdoor camping equipment are generally taxable supplies of goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French domestic VAT franchise regime applicable to ordinary sales of goods and commercial activities, the principal annual turnover threshold is EUR 85,000, subject to the statutory prior-year and current-year threshold tests and applicable indexed thresholds. Exceeding the relevant threshold removes the business from the franchise regime and may require VAT registration. The lower threshold applicable to services is generally EUR 37,500 and is not ordinarily relevant to the stated outdoor equipment retail activity. The franchise regime does not eliminate VAT obligations for imports, certain intra-Community transactions, or transactions subject to special rules. Cross-border B2C distance sales within the EU are generally subject to destination-country VAT once the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold is exceeded, unless OSS is used or another statutory rule applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all private-sector invoices. French domestic B2B e-invoicing is being introduced in phases: all French businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large enterprises and medium-sized enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2026; and small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2027, subject to statutory implementation rules and possible regulatory adjustments. Transmission is expected through the public platform or an accredited private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, or PDP). E-reporting obligations will apply to specified cross-border and B2C transactions. Invoices must satisfy French requirements for authenticity, integrity, legibility, mandatory content, and electronic preservation. General digital stamping is not required. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. VAT returns and payment are filed electronically through the DGFiP systems, with filing frequency determined by the applicable VAT regime and turnover.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the exporter can substantiate the export and the customs exit from the EU. The supplier must retain a valid commercial invoice, identify the customer and goods, use the correct customs procedure, and obtain reliable electronic evidence of exit, normally through the customs export declaration and exit results. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State are generally exempt with the right to deduct when the transport, customer VAT identification, and recapitulative reporting conditions are satisfied; they are not exports outside the EU. Services supplied to a business established outside France are generally governed by place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated. B2C services and services connected with goods require separate place-of-supply analysis. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, business-use evidence, and compliance with the relevant domestic, EU refund, or non-EU refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French customs export declaration and export accompanying document or equivalent electronic customs record
MRN (Movement Reference Number) and electronic confirmation of exit from the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, VAT treatment, and delivery terms
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, air waybill, consignment note, or courier export record as applicable
Proof of delivery or transport to the non-EU destination where required to corroborate customs evidence
Customs broker mandate and customs power of attorney where a representative files the export declaration
Import customs or destination-country entry evidence where available
Accounting records linking the export declaration, invoice, inventory movement, payment, and VAT return
Bank payment evidence where commercially available; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French VAT export document
Customer VAT identification and transport evidence for qualifying intra-Community supplies, where the transaction is within the EU rather than an export outside the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds applicable to this business. Export VAT exemption is subject to retrospective assessment if customs exit or transaction conditions are not substantiated. The administration may reassess unpaid VAT, deny input VAT recovery, charge late-payment interest, and impose tax penalties. A 10% penalty may generally apply for late payment or certain filing failures, with higher penalties for deliberate non-compliance, including 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to the facts and statutory safeguards. False invoices, concealment, or organized VAT fraud may create criminal exposure in addition to civil tax liabilities. Interest and penalties may apply from the original due date, and clawback may cover all affected reporting periods within the applicable limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the Eurosystem and in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment service providers is delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), and external finance and financial sanctions policy is administered via the Direction Générale du Trésor under the Code monétaire et financier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is a fully convertible currency for both current and capital account transactions; France has no exchange-control licensing regime for ordinary trade, dividends, loan servicing, or capital repatriation. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union guarantees free movement of capital, including profit remittances by non-resident shareholders of a French SARL, subject only to standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) compliance and, where applicable, dividend withholding tax relief under a double-taxation treaty. Balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the Banque de France applies only for declared cross-border financial relations above the statutory threshold (as adjusted by the Banque de France, generally EUR 1,000,000 of annual external flows); no prior administrative authorization or capital repatriation license is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist under French law. Export receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be retained in ordinary operational accounts or dedicated foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) at ACPR-licensed banks. The only mandatory obligations are (i) EU/AML controls on cash transactions above EUR 10,000 and suspicious-transaction reporting, (ii) Banque de France balance-of-payments declarations for financial relations with non-residents above the reporting threshold, and (iii) full compliance with EU/UN restrictive measures and sanctions screening of counterparties. Conversion of export receipts into EUR is permitted at market rates without prior approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account (compte courant) with optional segregated capital escrow/blocked contribution account (compte bloqué) for phased shareholder injections; full SWIFT, FX and trade-finance channel
Operational account with integrated e-banking, FX desk and trade-services; capital escrow account available for SARL incorporation funding
Operational account at the regional Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Épargne; capital escrow/compte bloqué available at incorporation
Operational account via the local caisse régionale; capital escrow account possible with slightly longer onboarding due to cooperative governance
Operational account and capital escrow option; onboarding viability depends on the local caisse's commercial appetite for low-ticket e-commerce SARLs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) that passport into France under PSD2 (for example a French-licensed EMI or a passported continental EMI with an ACPR-registered branch or agent), but Low for offshore digital EMIs domiciled outside the EEA (e.g., United Kingdom after Brexit, United States, Singapore or Hong Kong). Legal constraints: an offshore non-EEA EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts or e-money services to a French SARL without obtaining a French EMI licence, implementing an EEA passporting arrangement, or operating through a French-authorised payment institution agent. The Code monétaire et financier requires payment services to be rendered exclusively by licensed or passported institutions, and French banks retain the primary relationship for K-bis verification, UBO filings, credit facilities and balance-of-payments declaration. Recommended structure: main treasury account at a Tier-1 bank supplemented by an EEA-licensed EMI for high-frequency marketplace payouts and online card settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under French AML/KYC rules (Code monétaire et financier, Art. L561-5 and R561-5), the SARL's legal representative (gérant) or a duly mandated officer must provide certified identity documents, the K-bis/INPI extract, articles of association, and proof of the ultimate beneficial owner(s) at the 25% threshold. In-person physical appearance at a branch interview remains the prevailing standard for BNP Paribas, Société Générale and Crédit Agricole; non-resident gérants may alternatively attend a French consulate or provide notarized/apostilled copies with a remote eIDAS-qualified video interview, although many relationship managers still require one in-person signatory visit. Remote opening is fully viable for smaller banks and French/EEA-licensed digital banks that accept eIDAS signatures and video KYC; the French SARL structure with non-resident ownership is not a prohibitive factor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP (politically exposed person) or adverse-media hit on the gérant or any ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports, proof of residential address, tax residence certificates, judicial record extract (bulletin n°3), sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, written PEP-status explanation with mitigating evidence, an independent sanctions/PEP screening report (e.g., World-Check or LexisNexis) confirming no exact match, and the SARL's K-bis/INPI registration extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution or shareholder loan funded from a non-EEA jurisdiction, from cryptocurrency assets, or through an unidentifiable banking chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank attestation of the blocked capital account (attestation de blocage des fonds), statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) capital-contribution certificate when appointed, detailed bank statements tracing the injected EUR funds, notarized shareholder resolutions, signed articles of association, and a forensic accountant's letter confirming the absence of a money-laundering predicate offense.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marketplace payment flows from Stripe/PayPal characterized by rapid early turnover, elevated chargebacks, or bulk settlement entries not reconcilable with customer sales.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform payout and settlement reconciliation statements for at least 12 months, merchant verification letters from Stripe and PayPal, order/invoice/refund ledgers, logistics and customs declarations (bills of lading or SAD import/export declarations), an internal AML control procedure implementing Art. L561-2, and a written description of the e-commerce commercial model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments from or to high-risk third countries (FATF-monitored or EU-listed high-risk jurisdictions) or from customers with unverifiable beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence file per counterparty: registration certificates, proof of address, bank confirmation, underlying commercial contracts and invoices, export/import documentation, end-beneficiary attestations, and a documented transaction-monitoring and refusal policy aligned with the Code monétaire et financier and EU restrictive-measures regulations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing for shareholder capital: for EEA/EUR shareholders use SEPA Credit Transfer displaying the ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose code 'CAPC' (capital payment); for non-EEA shareholders use SWIFT MT103 with mandatory UETR (gpi) and a remittance reference containing the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for a direct investment/capital contribution, plus the text 'Capital Contribution FR SARL ISIC 4791'. The receiving bank will verify the K-bis extract, UBO declaration, articles of association, and the blocked-capital attestation if applicable. Aggregate inbound/outbound flows above the annual reporting threshold require Banque de France RF declarations; no prior exchange-control approval is required, but sanctions screening and source-of-funds verification apply. Capital increases must be recorded at the RCS/INPI and, where the contribution is in kind, verified by a commissaire aux apports.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails: for EEA suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfers (TARGET2-SCT) with structured remittance references and trade-related purpose codes; for non-EEA suppliers, SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV under the gpi standard with UETR and ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose codes 'TRAD' (trade) or 'PURC'/'GOOD' indicating goods purchase; for high-value or first-time supplier relationships, an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (payable at sight, UCP600) confirmed by a French/EEA bank, covering HS Chapter 94 camping/outdoor goods, with commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and SAD customs declaration aligned to the SARL's NAF/APE code 4791Z. Payment profiling tools at the bank can segregate trade disbursements from collection-cycle payouts to Stripe/PayPal.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) with maturities up to 24 months executed under the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement or ISDA 2002 with an ACPR-licensed or EEA-licensed credit institution, restricted to commercial hedging of the SARL's underlying trade exposures.

FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term liquidity bridging between EUR and foreign-currency positions, subject to EMIR trade reporting to an EU-registered trade repository where the non-financial counterparty structure applies.

Cross-currency swaps (swap de devises croisées) for aligning long-dated shareholder loans, leases or acquisition instruments denominated in EUR/USD/GBP, requiring an ISDA/CSA collateral arrangement and prior internal treasury-review approval.

Exchange-traded and OTC plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP options/futures for directional protection of large seasonal purchase orders, with mandatory ACPR suitability assessment and margining through a regulated clearing member.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically permissible only for restricted or non-convertible currencies (e.g., offshore CNY, INR, BRL) where deliverable interbank markets do not function; they are not required for fully convertible pairs such as EUR/USD or EUR/GBP and carry heightened regulatory documentation and valuation obligations under French banking practice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by associates within six months of fiscal year-end and filed with the registry within one month of approval; for a calendar-year SARL, approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 3,000 for the legal entity (EUR 1,500 for its manager) for late or non-filing; two consecutive years of non-filing may trigger administrative strike-off from the RCS or judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration de Résultats n°2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day after 1 May for fiscal year ending 31 December; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within two months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax due plus monthly late interest of 0.20%; a 10% surcharge applies if the balance is not paid within 30 days of notice, and enforced recovery may follow

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at fiscal year-end, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total balance sheet assets above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excluding VAT) above EUR 8,000,000; average employee count above 50. Minority shareholders may also request a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général — ANC Regulation 2014-03), harmonized with EU directives; IFRS as adopted by the EU only for consolidated listed groups or when permitted by law

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO filing; the beneficial owner declaration must be lodged with the registry at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change. As part of annual corporate secretarial maintenance, the SARL must internally verify that the Register of Beneficial Owners is accurate and that any share transfer or shareholder alteration was duly declared. Failure to update triggers criminal fines up to EUR 15,000 and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment of up to six months.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Director Decisions and Shareholders' Meetings (Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–18,000 (EUR 3,500–16,000) dependent on transaction volume, controls, and IT environment
